issues.detail: The contains regex 'supersed|invalidat|stale|replac|no longer' is a necessary condition. The template's own wording ('superseded result', 'Replace invalidated evidence') makes a match likely, but a correct run could write 'outdated', 'obsolete', 'out of date', or 'does not apply to the current content' and still fail.
issues.fix: In tester-3/spec.json, checks[1].all[1].contains.regex: broaden to 'supersed|invalidat|stale|replac|no longer|outdated|out of date|obsolete|not current|does not (?:apply|support)|rerun|re-run'. Keep the selfCheck that greps the original report for the same pattern in sync, and confirm the original report still contains none of the words. The original text 'Not yet run' does not contain 'rerun' or 're-run'.

issues.detail: The 'status-filtered' literal relies on the Tester keeping that phrase when it rewrites the budget table. It matches the test name, so the phrase will very likely survive anywhere S1 is cited. Because complete is false, a judge still decides preservation.
Git author is 'Fixture <fixture@example.invalid>' and every commit has the same timestamp. These are visible in git log and faintly hint at a test repository. Both are harness-wide builder defaults.

Nothing records who made the unstaged src change, and Developer's plan self-checks cite only commit 0bebb8d. A correct Tester might note this, or ask whether the change belongs to the cycle. The case's expected output (reconcile under REVERIFY) still holds, and the judge can grade either reasonable handling.

summary: Every stated condition is realized: the interrupted VERIFY report records S1 passing and S2 unrun with blob identities, the source and fixture changes are unstaged and differ from those identities, and scope and design are unchanged, all proven by selfChecks. check.mjs is ok and the invariants fit a Tester; HEAD, git mutation, check_ok, and implementation and upstream records unchanged still leave test files free.
